title: 1958 AHSME Problem 34
statement: The numerator of a fraction is \(6x+1,\) the denominator is \(7-4x,\) and \(x\) can have any value between \(-2\) and \(2,\) both included. The values of \(x\) for which the numerator is greater than the denominator are:

solutions.text:
The required comparison gives \[ 6x+1\gt7-4x, \] so \(10x\gt6\) and \(x\gt\frac{3}{5}.\) Intersecting this with \(-2\le x\le2\) gives \[ \frac35\lt x\le2. \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Compare the numerator and denominator directly by solving \(6x+1\gt7-4x\)
Intersect the resulting inequality with the given interval \([-2,2]\)
